headline: H-Spec removes the separate drafter KV cache in parallel speculative decoding
summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv paper introduces H-Spec, a parallel speculative-decoding drafter that combines Mamba state initialized from the target model’s last-position hidden state with attention that reuses the target KV cache in place. This removes a separate drafter-side KV cache. Under the authors’ matched training recipe, H-Spec reports 5.0–13.3% higher mean accepted length and 5.3–12.6% higher batch-size-1 inter-token-latency speedup than the best baseline across three targets and eight tasks, with paired bootstrap 95% intervals above zero. On one NVIDIA A100 80G using vLLM, the paper reports higher throughput and lower KV-cache utilization across concurrency 8–128. These remain author-reported results; the paper notes slower drafting below concurrency 32 and initially on shorter inputs, and requires matching drafter and target K/V dimensions. Independent serving reproduction and transfer beyond the measured setup remain open.
